messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] GPU_POOL_HIGH_QUEUE inference-prod: queue_len=1124, queued_seconds_p50=12.3, hpa_target_replicas=0, last_scaled=12m ago. source=prometheus-adapter, severity=high

sara: i'm oncall. seeing the alert. paging oncall — i'm looking. anyone oncall for infra? :eyes:

mike: infra here. digging into autoscaler metrics now. quick summary from the grafana panel — GPU node count steady, pod replicas flat, backlog growing. annotations show adapter scrape lag ~ 45s then jump to 6m.

danielle: ml-sre — we started seeing model-serving queue growth ~15m ago after a rollout to v2. Not sure if rollout changed rps. FWIW error rates are 502->503 ramping.

lia: support — customers A, B reported timeouts and 5xxs starting ~18:10 UTC. raised ticket #CUST-1289.

kevin: paged from PD. oncall handoff in 10. i'll take first responder if no objections.

sara: ok kevin you have it. i'll coordinate customer comms and triage. mike/danielle, what telemetry should we collect first?

mike: grab these: `kubectl get hpa -n inference`, `kubectl get pods -l app=inference -o wide`, nodepool GPU utilization, and `prometheus-adapter` logs. also check `custom.metrics.k8s.io` availability.

danielle: running queries now. prom query: `sum(kafka_consumer_group_lag{topic="request-queue"})` -> 1.2e3. `sum(gpu_memory_used_bytes)` looks normal. it's queue backlog not memory.

kevin: attendees — i'm going to mute PD after we confirm mitigations. any quick mitigation we can do without risking correctness?

mike: immediate mitigation — scale up nodepool manually and scale inference replicas while we fix metric pipeline. i can request +8 GPUs from infra pool (estimated 4-6m to spin up).

sara: do it. also enable fallback model (lite) for public traffic to reduce per-request GPU time. danielle can we flip traffic?

danielle: yes, we have a canary route. issuing `POST /control/route` to shift 30% -> lite variant. will do now.

deploy-bot: Deployment v2.3.1-lite-route: rolling canary started by danielle at 18:28 UTC.

mike: infra request submitted: `gcloud container node-pools resize inference-gpu-pool --num-nodes=22` (current 14 -> 22). ETA 5-7m.

sara: customers: lia please send short update: we're aware, mitigating, expected partial relief within 10m.

lia: message posted to affected customers and status page. :white_check_mark:

danielle: prom adapter logs show repeated `500` when querying `custom.metrics.k8s.io`:
```
E0401 18:22:11.123 adapter.go:210] error listing metrics: context deadline exceeded
E0401 18:23:05.987 adapter.go:210] error listing metrics: downstream unavailable
```
Looks like prometheus-adapter or kube-metrics-server struggling to serve the custom metrics. HPA can't see request queue metric.

mike: that explains no scaling. is prometheus server healthy?

danielle: prometheus scraping healthy, but adapter to k8s API has high error rate. checking recently applied RBAC changes.

kevin: timeline check: alert fired 18:26. queue growth started ~18:10. rollout at 18:05. prometheus-adapter errors began ~18:20. so likely combo: slightly higher load from rollout + adapter lag = autoscaler blind spot and then queue explosion.

mike: manual scaling in place now: scaled inference deployment from 64 -> 96 replicas to drain queue. nodepool still scaling. watching QPS and 95p latency.

sara: any immediate customer impact metrics?

danielle: reduced 5xx rate from 4.2% -> 1.6% after canary and manual scale, still above baseline 0.1%. queue length trending down from 1.1k -> 450 in last 6m.

lia: customers confirmed partial recovery, some still seeing errors under heavy load. status page updated 18:36 UTC.

mike: prom-adapter pod restarted by me (evicted crashloop). after restart adapter backfilling metrics; HPA saw metrics at 18:35 and attempted a scale but was capped by nodepool before manual scale finished.

kevin: any change to alerts? should we mute the noisy ones?

sara: keep high-severity alerts. mute the duplicate queue growth warning for 10m to reduce noise.

danielle: follow-up items to add to postmortem: 1) adapter RBAC/health checks & automated restart policy 2) HPA fallback behavior when custom metrics unavailable (e.g., use CPU as fallback for short window) 3) rollout prechecks for rps/latency impact 4) nodepool warm capacity for burst scaling

mike: i'll add infra action: reduce nodepool spin-up time and add capacity buffer for critical pools.

kevin: closing loop — manual mitigation appears to have stabilized service. queue under 200 now, 95p latency trending down. i will handover back to sara at 18:48 UTC.

sara: thanks team. we'll run a blameless postmortem. assigning owners: danielle for adapter root cause, mike for infra capacity, kevin for oncall playbook updates, lia for customer follow-up.

lia: i've updated the ticket with the mitigation timeline and customers notified.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: status=stabilized, responders=[kevin,sara,mike,danielle], summary="Prometheus-adapter lag caused HPA blindness -> GPU pool queue growth; mitigated via manual scaling and canary fallback". Postmortem assigned.

sara: filing the incident with links to dashboards and logs. will send invites for the blameless postmortem tomorrow. :pray:
